record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: Develop a Fundamental Theorem for PEPS in two and higher dimensions that applies to the largest possible class of projected entangled pair states, bridging the currently understood normal case and the fully general case where equality of generated states is undecidable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on a two-dimensional lattice is specified by a local tensor $A \in \mathbb{C}^{d \otimes D^{\otimes 4}}$ (physical dimension $d$, virtual bond dimension $D$); contracting copies of $A$ along the bonds of an $n\times n$ torus produces a family of states $\{|\psi_n(A)\rangle\}_{n\ge 1}$. A PEPS tensor $A$ is called normal if there exists some region size $R$ such that the blocked tensor on every $R\times R$ patch is injective as a linear map from the virtual indices to the physical indices.

For Matrix Product States and for normal PEPS, a "Fundamental Theorem" is known: two tensors $A$ and $B$ generate the same family of states $|\psi_n(A)\rangle = |\psi_n(B)\rangle$ for all sufficiently large $n$ if and only if $A$ and $B$ are related by a gauge transformation on the virtual indices. On the other hand, for fully general PEPS, deciding whether two tensors generate the same family of states is algorithmically undecidable, so no constructive Fundamental Theorem can hold in full generality.

Problem. Formulate and prove a Fundamental Theorem for PEPS in two and higher spatial dimensions that applies to the largest possible class $\mathcal{C}$ of PEPS tensors strictly larger than the class of normal PEPS: identify an explicit, verifiable structural condition defining $\mathcal{C}$, and characterize, for $A, B \in \mathcal{C}$, the precise (gauge-type) relations between $A$ and $B$ that are equivalent to the equality $|\psi_n(A)\rangle = |\psi_n(B)\rangle$ for all sufficiently large lattice sizes $n$. The class $\mathcal{C}$ should be as broad as possible, interpolating between the normal case and the undecidable fully general case.
artifact.status_search_result: A Fundamental Theorem is established for normal PEPS, and partial extensions exist: notably, a Fundamental Theorem has been proved for the class of semi-injective PEPS (covering e.g. AKLT and CZX ground states), giving necessary and sufficient conditions for two tensors to generate the same family of 2D states. However, a full Fundamental Theorem covering the maximal possible subclass beyond these results is not known, and it is established that the fully general PEPS equality problem is algorithmically undecidable, so the problem remains only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: A generalization of the injectivity condition for Projected Entangled Pair States (semi-injective PEPS)
status_evidence.snippet: Parent Hamiltonians can be constructed for which semi-injective PEPS are unique ground states, and necessary and sufficient conditions for two tensors to generate the same family of such states in two spatial dimensions have been determined.
status_evidence.claim: A Fundamental Theorem is known for semi-injective PEPS, a strict extension of the normal/injective class.

status_evidence.title: PEPS: Fundamental Analytical and Numerical Limitations
status_evidence.snippet: The question whether a PEPS has a certain symmetry is undecidable—there is no algorithm which, given a PEPS tensor, can ever decide whether the family of states generated by that tensor will be symmetric.
status_evidence.claim: For fully general PEPS the equivalence/symmetry decision problem is undecidable, so a Fundamental Theorem cannot exist in full generality.

status_evidence.title: MPS and PEPS: Concepts, Symmetries, and Theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive review of Fundamental Theorems for MPS and normal PEPS, with open problems on extending to larger classes.
status_evidence.claim: Fundamental Theorems are established for normal PEPS; broader extensions remain open.
